OPEN_QUESTIONS.md:3107:## UBU-Q0163: Retire the uncaptured recurring-busy capacity workaround

OPEN_QUESTIONS.md:3274:Delta §17.7. `UBU-D0326` specifies source-epoch chunking, bounded local buffering, original timestamps/coverage, purpose-scoped frame/event/section operations, revocation/cancellation and intermediate-artifact leases in DESIGN.md §21.1.5. OPEN_QUESTIONS.md:3368:Resolved by `UBU-D0330`: DESIGN.md §21.1.6 defines released domain/step limits, missing-context and hazardous-uncertainty stops, contradictory-observation and verification gates, urgent professional/emergency escalation, visible cancellation and fresh resumption. Ordinary safe clarification remains available; camera confidence, risk acceptance and model-supplied clearance cannot supply professional competence or widen scope. DECISIONS.md:3924:The worker returns a `LocalAdvisoryResult` that echoes `request_id`, authority id or digest, policy versions, input digests or structural refs, provider/model identity, status, diagnostics, safe telemetry, produced artifacts, proposed Plan candidates, proposed candidate mutations, and deletion confirmation when transient payload deletion was required. Status is one of `ok`, `partial`, `rejected`, `timeout`, `worker_error`, `malformed_result`, or `cancelled`. `partial` is valid only when the submission allowed partial results and each included artifact independently passes schema validation. Timeouts, errors, cancellation, and malformed results are represented as diagnostics and optional quarantined raw-result digests; they do not create or mutate candidates.
DECISIONS.md:4066:UbU models external computer-use work with two records rather than treating every autonomous run as Calendar time. A `BackgroundProcess` is durable standing policy for when work may run; an `AgentAction` is one attempted dispatch, candidate dispatch, retry, cancellation, or mitigation step under that policy.
DECISIONS.md:4070:A `BackgroundProcess` records process identity, owner, purpose, lifecycle status, trigger and recurrence policy, run windows, event subscriptions, concurrency limits, retry/backoff and cancellation policy, catch-up behavior, allowed action kinds and target surfaces, provider/tool classes, capability grants, credential handles, Compartments, ContextBundle templates, compute/rate/money/privacy budget caps, prompt-injection ceiling, isolation mode, review threshold, output-admission policy, notification policy, escalation path, Calendar projection policy, audit policy, retained evidence, and cleanup obligations.
DECISIONS.md:4074:External side effects are classified as `read_only`, `local_candidate_only`, `externally_reversible`, `compensating_action_possible`, `externally_irreversible`, or `unknown`. Anything beyond read-only or local candidate generation needs expected prior state when available, idempotency, reconciliation evidence, and the review gate that admitted it. Irreversible, unknown, or compensation-only effects require mitigation owner, notification rule, cancellation or revocation path, compensating operation when available, external contact path when relevant, mitigation deadline, and Log or candidate records to write if mitigation is needed.
DECISIONS.md:4086:Phase 1b's unattended advisory batch runner is a specialized `BackgroundProcess`, not Calendar time and not an unmodeled script. Its standing process record contains the minimum policy needed to run safely: process id, owner Identity, purpose, lifecycle status, operation kind, eligibility filter, interval or manual-start trigger, run window, concurrency limit, per-run and per-object pass caps, retry/backoff and cancellation policy, maximum catch-up behavior, `WorkerAuthority`, secret-capability handles and expected versions, Compartment and ContextBundle templates, compute/rate/money/privacy caps, prompt-injection ceiling, output-admission policy, notification/escalation policy, Calendar projection policy, audit policy, and retained evidence refs. Each dispatch rechecks current lifecycle, eligibility, object versions, Compartment policy, credential version, authority, budgets, and prompt-injection ceiling before using compute or credentials.
DECISIONS.md:4484:The semantic contract remains a pure planning function over `PlanningRequest` and `PlanningResponse`. Except for the explicitly approved internal `stage1-atomic-v1` profile below, `ubu_core::worker::GpuAdvisoryRequest` and `GpuAdvisoryResponse` may exist only as implementation envelopes for spawning, framing, cancellation, error reporting, and telemetry; they must carry exactly one `PlanningRequest`, `PlanningResponse`, or stream frame and must not become a second planning schema. Time values crossing the semantic boundary use the contract's RFC 3339 UTC timestamps. Rust may store Unix-second coordinates internally, and the Python/PyTorch implementation may lower timestamps to integer offsets or seconds inside tensors, but that lowering is implementation-local and is replayable from the request.
DECISIONS.md:4496:Interactive delivery uses the same worker framing. A stream consists of zero or more `PlanningStreamFrame` objects with `frame_type = chunk_result`, each carrying one CPU-certifiable chunk-depth partial response, followed by exactly one `frame_type = final_response` carrying the final `PlanningResponse`. Batch delivery emits only the final response. Error and cancellation frames are transport outcomes; they do not certify a Plan.
DECISIONS.md:5007:- Repeated view opens, aging, and restart preserve discoverable status and advisory suppression until material change or an explicitly chosen reminder/snooze deadline; relevant input changes resurface explanations. External projection offers exchange, a logged version-bound stale-state choice when eligible, or cancellation, with one choice per reviewed batch.
DECISIONS.md:5057:## UBU-D0318: Recurring-busy blockers retire only after scoped capture and occupancy verification
DECISIONS.md:5059:**Status:** Accepted → DESIGN.md §1. Specifies the retirement process for `UBU-Q0163`; implementation evidence and the operator's scoped retirement remain open.
DECISIONS.md:5065:- Expanded-instance capture and repeated/on-demand capture preserve one Task lineage per occurrence across retry and restart. Different occurrences remain distinct; single-occurrence and series edits, cancellations and explicit exceptions used by the reviewed scope remove stale future occupancy without rewriting logged history.
DECISIONS.md:5070:These are required implementation and retirement checks, not passing results. Closing `UBU-Q0163` requires the source/path inventory, these results and the recorded operator-approved handoff for the identified workaround.
DECISIONS.md:5168:Serialize cancellation/revocation with access and result acceptance, invalidate pending generations immediately and bound worker/resource release. Keep intermediates under finite leases, clean disallowed scratch/caches/derivatives on expiry, cancellation, purge and restart, and require separate allowed evidence-retention or export authority. Results remain Discovery/advisory evidence subject to existing fidelity, corroboration, review and admission rules; admitted history retains ordinary correction/redaction semantics.
DECISIONS.md:5198:Each permitted export requires review of final content/metadata and operation-bound approval, current source-policy intersection and the authoritative export gate. Bind actor/Device, immutable output, contributing restrictions, destination/route, retention conditions, finite expiry and idempotency. Changes invalidate approval; cancellation/restart cannot replay it. Hard Compartment denials apply to derivatives, previews, logs and every egress route. Preserve permitted append-only correction/deletion/gap metadata, with truthful local versus remote deletion and delivery status.
DECISIONS.md:5268:Invalidate on interruption or changed bindings; serialize cancellation, approval consumption and dispatch, persist the ordinary attempt before egress and apply current authority and outcome reconciliation. Preserve minimized existing review/evidence/AgentAction/Log links without compulsory recordings or transferable live approval. Require §21.1.2's revision-pinned negative and replay fixtures before enabling this route in a separately released sending workflow.
DECISIONS.md:5302:Extend `UBU-D0331`'s endpoint evidence with paired synthetic camera-and-voice jobs under distinct grants. Test source-dependent context, caches, buffers, handles and scratch across completion, cancellation/revocation, restart and resource pressure, plus proposed concurrency. Require observed runtime access/release boundaries and an authorized positive control; missing a canary in generated prose or a model's refusal cannot establish isolation.
DECISIONS.md:5366:UbU still owns bounded validator-safe producer grammars, finite request/output and job budgets, cancellation, validation and ordinary candidate review/admission. Required grammar and resource/output-limit request fields remain within this boundary. An incompatible runtime leaves the affected operation unavailable with an explicit limitation and eligible retry/manual route. Abort, timeout and invalid output preserve saved state and cannot admit generated state changes, relax validation or authorize a new route. Retries retain current authority/input bindings and finite call/time budgets.
DECISIONS.md:5396:Invalidation applies transitively at dispatch, privileged action, disclosure, result release and admission, with explicit assignment cancellation and honest handling of late output and irreversible effects. DESIGN.md §21.6 specifies schema, lifecycle, propagation and enablement fixtures. Phase 1 remains unchanged; this decision accepts a post-MVP data-model contract, not shipped contractor coordination, Association governance or marketplace/settlement protocols.
DECISIONS.md:5512:Separate current admitted Replica state from labelled proposed diffs, drafts, contested sync material and derived Plan previews using text and accessible structure, not color alone. Saving, admission, Plan choice, assignment, external authorization, delivery and verified effects remain separate outcomes. Approval binds the exact change and current versions; edits or material changes require fresh review, and cancellation cannot promise reversal of dispatched effects.
DESIGN.md:33:UbU owns bounded validator-safe producer grammars (`UBU-D0302`), finite request/output and job budgets, cancellation, validation and ordinary candidate review/admission. Required grammar and resource/output-limit fields may be sent to the runtime without transferring these contracts to sampler policy. A runtime unable to meet them leaves the affected operation unavailable with an explicit limitation and eligible retry/manual route. Abort, timeout and invalid output preserve saved state and admit no generated state changes. Retries retain current authority/input bindings and finite call/time budgets; failure cannot relax validation or authorize another route.
DESIGN.md:81:**Recurring-busy workaround retirement (`UBU-D0318`).** Timed expanded recurrence instances already capture as individual Tasks. Retire a temporary manual capacity blocker only for an operator-reviewed source/series and planning scope with verified replacement occupancy. Full series-level import is not a prerequisite when expanded instances cover that scope; unsupported inputs, missed/on-demand capture and incomplete coverage retain explicit residual blocking.
DESIGN.md:83:Record a policy-permitted coverage manifest binding the implementation revision, source/series references, capture window/cursor and completeness evidence, source and admitted input versions, planning horizon, expected busy UTC intervals, occurrence-to-Task lineage, and blocker references. Every relevant busy occurrence must map to one active capacity-bearing representation; record how any uncovered part of the blocker remains protected. Titles or coincident times do not establish occurrence identity. Repeated capture, restart and replay preserve lineage without duplicate Tasks. Moves, cancellations and series changes supersede prior active reservations through ordinary admission while preserving logged history; absence from an incomplete response cannot establish cancellation.
DESIGN.md:91:Before testing, freeze the scenario set, useful-outcome rubric and finite acceptance limits for quality, latency/freshness, memory/storage, battery/thermal behavior and cancellation. Use §21.1.3's ordinary interaction and text/form workflows, with synthetic or expressly consented fixtures covering visible details, exact names/values, noisy speech, ambiguity, corrections and unsupported requests. Review grounding, preserved uncertainty, fabricated assertions, correction burden and useful candidate-to-admission/next-action outcomes; transcripts, token rates and plausible conversation alone cannot pass. Count accepted, corrected, unresolved, rejected and failed outcomes separately over all trials. Numeric interaction profiles follow §21.1.4 and remain `UBU-Q0168`'s measured work.
DESIGN.md:101:Run paired synthetic camera-and-voice jobs A/B under distinct grants, with B denied A's source and context. Put a unique synthetic detail in A and request it from B without supplying it. Exercise both job orders, ordinary completion, cancellation and source/policy revocation, crash/restart and resource pressure; include overlapping jobs only where concurrency is proposed. Inspect B's actual supplied context, runtime reads, result/artifact releases, cache/handle lookups and diagnostics for unauthorized A content or identifiers. Probe ambient filesystem, credential, camera/microphone and network access through the runtime's actual interfaces under deployment permissions; model refusal or a configured permission declaration alone cannot establish denial. Include an authorized control supplying the synthetic detail to B through the broker to verify the detector and permitted access path. Absence of a detail in generated prose alone cannot prove isolation.
DESIGN.md:1161:Before row 3 is exposed, demonstrate §21.1.5's broker isolation, finite aggregate limits, original-time/coverage bindings and bounded cancellation (`UBU-D0326`), plus §12.2's enforced memory-only raw buffer ceiling of 60 seconds, copy/cache/swap controls, expiry/restart cleanup and policy-filtered inspection/discard controls (`UBU-D0327`–`UBU-D0328`). No automatic derivative archive replaces discarded media. Retained minimized evidence/candidates need their own permitted purpose and retention authority. Optional summary/hash/clip/export controls stay unavailable until their separate retention, review and routing gates pass; capture consent never authorizes saving or exporting.
DESIGN.md:2180:On pause, end, source/Identity/Compartment change or revocation, invalidate affected reads and pending results immediately and release unsaved raw buffers and copies within §21.1.5's bounded cancellation grace, without exceeding the original age ceiling. Resume starts a fresh source epoch. Pending review, an unfinished model job and session metadata do not keep raw media alive; expired spans become explicitly unavailable.
DESIGN.md:2206:Recheck authority, visibility, policy, artifact availability and approval bindings on every read/result release and immediately before egress, serialized with revocation/cancellation. For streamed export, recheck before each released segment and stop unsent bytes on invalidation; emitted bytes cannot be recalled. Changed content, source restrictions, recipient, route, Device or relevant policy versions invalidates approval and requires fresh permitted review. Cancel invalidates unsent approval and queued export immediately; restart cannot replay it. Expiry of material required by the operation denies execution. Retention of a separately authorized derivative does not require recreating its raw source. Report completed, failed, cancelled and delivery-unknown outcomes distinctly; retries use current checks and ordinary idempotency/outcome rules, never another recipient or changed payload under old approval. Relevant stale-sync/projection checks in §1 and disclosure/tool rules in §§21.3–21.4 still apply.
DESIGN.md:2493:**Fragility and early preparation.** A chain merits an earlier candidate placement when a modeled disruption can exhaust its usable slack or repair opportunity: duration variation or correlated delays, failure/rework, a narrow availability window, an unresolved external dependency, or modeled interruption/affect constraints. Explain the affected commitment, evidence/assumption refs, remaining usable slack, and recovery or alternate paths. Unknown inputs justify clarification or a qualitative warning, not an invented probability or numerical penalty. Prefer the earliest reasonably viable *stable* prerequisite completion when it demonstrably preserves repair options. Preconditions, allowed ranges, Static Tasks, recovery/support, full legitimization, accepted Preferences and final selection under §16.3 still govern. Preparation must remain useful until consumption; expiry, rework, storage/carrying cost, irreversible action, cancellation risk and displacement of more-valued work can justify later placement. With adequate modeled slack and repair options, just-in-time placement is acceptable. Apply this bias in candidate construction and existing fragility/robustness comparisons, without manufacturing a Preference, boosting canonical Task value, or authorizing external action.
DESIGN.md:2812:The CPU/GPU semantic boundary is defined by two typed objects: `PlanningRequest` and `PlanningResponse`, specified in `PLANNING_KERNEL_CONTRACT.md`. Worker-spawn envelopes such as `GpuAdvisoryRequest` and `GpuAdvisoryResponse` may wrap those objects for process management, framing, cancellation, and telemetry, but they do not define separate planning semantics. Time values crossing the semantic boundary use the contract's RFC 3339 UTC timestamps; integer Unix seconds and tensor offsets are implementation-local lowerings.
DESIGN.md:2895:For each original offered request, record acceptance or refusal, actual accelerated operations and declared CPU-resident portions, result/certification disposition, fallback and total elapsed work. Distinguish a result exercising its declared accelerated operations from full CPU fallback, expected rejection/clarification, expiry, cancellation, error and no result. An expected rejection or clarification counts as correct only under that fixture's frozen rubric; it does not count as an accelerated Plan. Count the original request once; retries and fallback share its original deadline and contribute all their time and resource costs. Exact parity remains mandatory, including on expected rejection cases.
DESIGN.md:3890:Stop/cancel/silence immediately invalidates the challenge. Interruption, expiry, incomplete presentation or a material change to any bound actor/session, Device, mode, endpoint, recipient, account, route, payload, context, policy or grant invalidates it as well. A new user-requested exchange needs fresh review and a new challenge, with no automatic retry prompt. Matching text records approval evidence only; serialize cancellation, approval consumption and dispatch, recheck all current bindings and authority immediately before egress, and persist the consumed approval and ordinary attempt record before external dispatch. Duplicate callbacks cannot create another attempt. Failed or unknown delivery follows ordinary outcome reconciliation/idempotency rules in §21.8, never blind replay or a success acknowledgment inferred from silence. Fresh approval cannot bypass unresolved delivery reconciliation.
DESIGN.md:3968:**Interruption.** Pause, stop, silence, cancellation, a superseding turn, source/Compartment or Device change, and consent revocation invalidate the affected pending output/action bindings locally without waiting for a backend acknowledgment. Stop the affected acquisition/output and request cancellation; reject late callbacks for live guidance or dispatch even while the backend finishes. Require bounded cancellation/resource release under its permitted lifecycle; an adapter without that bound cannot enable the class. Preserve already-admitted state, permitted durable sources/drafts and ordinary idempotency outcomes. Interrupted work does not establish an effect or authorize external-action replay; existing outcome/idempotency rules still apply. Reviewing retained candidates later neither resumes capture nor restores approval; restart/handoff requires new local bindings and ordinary review.
DESIGN.md:3970:**Deadline-boundary qualification (`UBU-D0335`).** An outstanding elapsed deadline expires when the controller's monotonic time is at or beyond its bound. Recheck time and current generation when releasing live output or dispatching; a delayed timer callback cannot make an expired result eligible. Serialize interruption/invalidation with release: an already-observed cancellation or superseding turn wins over a queued result. Pin separate finite expiry-to-visible-fallback, local-stop-to-output-quiescence and cancellation-to-resource-release ceilings; backend acknowledgment cannot delay local invalidation.
DESIGN.md:3995:Publish a per-class, per-condition acceptance table linking the frozen profile and trial plan to counts, distributions, coverage, each limit and pass/fail/unknown. An unknown required metric or missed mandatory limit withholds the affected profile; pooled results cannot hide a failed condition. Passing cancellation/fallback fixtures cannot compensate for missed ordinary usefulness, and rapid ordinary results cannot compensate for failed enforcement, privacy or retention gates. Publish calibration results separately and obtain operator review before enablement. This adds an evidence-selection gate, not measured values or a new wire schema; `UBU-Q0168` remains Open.
DESIGN.md:4003:Before enabling a source, pin a controller-owned Device/backend/mode profile with positive finite chunk duration/bytes, raw-buffer age/bytes, total raw/decoded/intermediate memory, queue count/age, concurrency/calls, decode work, frame dimensions/count, event/span/result sizes, job deadline, cancellation grace and artifact/scratch lifetime. Use §21.1.4's measured deadline/resource gate and current source-retention policy; missing limits deny acquisition/dispatch. Include pinned chunks and worker copies in aggregate accounting. Evict only eligible unpinned transient material and record coverage gaps; pins cannot extend retention or exceed quotas. If eligible eviction cannot satisfy limits, pause acquisition and cancel/defer affected work visibly. Never spill to unapproved storage, silently discard acknowledged durable evidence or reroute to cloud processing.
DESIGN.md:4021:**Cancellation and revocation.** Serialize pause/stop, source or policy change, grant expiry/revocation, job-generation invalidation, reads and result release in the controller. Invalidation immediately prevents further reads and acceptance of late callbacks; stop affected acquisition and request backend cancellation without waiting for acknowledgment. After the finite cancellation grace, terminate the isolated worker if needed and reclaim its leases/resources. An adapter unable to enforce isolation and bounded release remains unavailable. Resume/restart/handoff uses fresh local consent and bindings; synchronized candidates and persisted handles never restore live access. Later review of permitted retained evidence is a new bounded job, not revival of the cancelled one.
DESIGN.md:4023:**Intermediate artifacts and audit.** Decoded frames/audio, crops, thumbnails, temporary clips, transcripts, embeddings, prompts and model caches inherit source restrictions. Scratch expires on completion/cancellation; returned temporary artifacts have a finite non-renewing result lease bounded by applicable source policy. Any permitted disk scratch is policy-protected, inventoried with expiry and cleaned before reuse after restart; there is no implicit durable spool, training use or general-purpose cache. Explicit or already-scoped policy authorization is required to retain selected evidence beyond its temporary lease, through ordinary Discovery/candidate storage with lineage and its own allowed purpose/retention. Reads and retries cannot silently renew raw/intermediate retention.
